source.title: Unlearning Isn't Deletion: Investigating Reversibility of Machine Unlearning in LLMs
source.authors: XiaoYu Xu; Xiang Yue; Yang Liu; Qing-Qing Ye; Hua-Di Zheng; Pei-Zhao Hu; Min-Xin Du; Hai-Bo Hu

record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests post-unlearning recovery with fine-tuning, quantization, and prompt-based interventions, using its own unlearning and representation-analysis protocols.
record.gate_note: The paper also describes attacks and results from cited studies; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Its PCA, CKA, and Fisher diagnostics are reported as evidence about representational drift, not as activation-direction ablations.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own unlearning (GA, NPO, RLabel, RMU, UnDIAL, AltPO, PDU, WAGLE) on Yi-6B, Qwen and Llama models. It then tests recovery by fine-tuning on forget, retain and unrelated data (B), Int4 quantization (D), and paraphrase, jailbreak and in-context prompting (E). It also uses PCA, CKA and FIM analyses to argue that forgetting is suppression rather than deletion (C).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that task-level metrics mislead: apparent forgetting is often reversible suppression with recoverable representations, and only parameter-updating relearning reliably restores it. Recovery depends on data source (forget set fastest, retain and unrelated slower). Quantization, prompting, jailbreak and in-context attacks fail in their GA setting, which they call reversible catastrophic forgetting. Irreversible, non-catastrophic forgetting is rarely achieved, with WAGLE under constrained relearning a 'seemingly' irreversible case.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses its own GA, NPO, RLabel, and other unlearning configurations, then evaluates constrained fine-tuning, Int4 quantization, prompt/jailbreak methods, in-context demonstrations, and representation diagnostics rather than reproducing one original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery changes with relearning data source and amount, learning rate, number of unlearning requests, unlearning method, and model. The paper reports stronger recovery from forget-set data than retain or unrelated data.

fits_no_version.finding: Pre-relearning mean PCA distance predicts whether relearning will restore accuracy (small at 3e-6/5e-6 means recoverable; large at 3e-5 means irreversible).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation drift before relearning predicts the reversibility of unlearning.

fits_no_version.finding: Relearning on the forget set after moderate continual unlearning exceeds original F.Acc (e.g., 83.8 vs 78.9 for NPO+KL).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning followed by relearning can improve forget-set performance above the original.

fits_no_version.finding: Min-k% MIA AUC rebounds to high values after relearning even when capability is permanently lost.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probability-based MIA misreports unlearning status under aggressive unlearning.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The authors note experiments cover multiple models but only a handful of tasks and methods, with validation on larger models and production-scale pipelines still needed. The tested recovery attacks in Table 11 are limited to one model and one GA setting; the claim-level attack comparison is not shown across the full model and method grid.
record.rows_left_out: Other Table 15 method-by-learning-rate combinations are not individually catalogued; the selected rows preserve the moderate-rate recovery pattern and the aggressive-rate partial-recovery pattern. Numerous task-level, PCA, CKA, and Fisher plots in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A.7 are not itemized because they are not direct attack-recovery outcomes; figure-only diagnostic values are described only where the text supplies a qualitative result.

untested.parts: No method is shown to reach near-chance targeted accuracy with preserved utility and then face the full attack battery. WAGLE keeps utility, but F.Acc stays at ~48 and it is tested only against retain and unrelated relearning.
Only Int4, on one GA setting in a catastrophic regime. Other bit widths and utility-preserving methods (NPO, RMU, etc.) are not tested.
Only one paraphrase, a fixed jailbreak prefix, and 5-shot in-context prompting, all on one catastrophic GA setting. Other languages and adaptive jailbreaks are not tested.
No robust counter-method is proposed or tested against the attack suite. WAGLE resisting constrained relearning is reported, but not as a robustness claim against all attacks.

missing.what: GA and others continual unlearning on Yi-6B. Moderate LR: unlearn 9.1 → relearn 80.0. LR 3e-5, N=100: relearn F.Acc 2.1, R.Acc 1.8.
GA continual unlearning on Qwen3-8B-Base, Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-3B. At 6e-6 relearning recovers 79.72/76.49/79.61. At 5e-5 it stays at 0.03/0.02/3.58.
GA+GD+WAGLE on Yi-6B: retain relearn 37.8→46.9; unrelated relearn 27.8→31.5; forget PCA distance stays large.
Qwen3-14B and Llama-3-8B-Instruct, GA/NPO: relearning recovers at 3e-6/5e-6 but not at 6e-5 (e.g., GA 2.3→4.5).
Mean PCA distance and CKA collapse at LR 3e-5 and are not recovered after relearning.
Single unlearning, six methods: relearning restores F.Acc to ~76–79, but unlearned F.Acc is not near chance (58–78).
Complex math task on Qwen2.5-7B: relearning recovers GSM8K at 3e-6/5e-6 (N=6) but not at 3e-5 or N=100.
Cross-lingual (Traditional Chinese) relearning reduces forget PCA distance partially; no accuracy is reported.

record.verdict_notes: D and E failures come from one GA setting with collapsed general ability, so I labelled them limits_scope rather than challenges. r8–r12 are representation diagnostics of attacks and relearning, not evidence on C. The record's C 'challenges' label misreads a regime the paper calls reversible. Much of the B evidence (Tables 3, 5, 7–10) is not in the rows.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report a condition that jointly brings targeted performance near chance, preserves general ability, and tests whether simple attacks then fail.
Fine-tuning on a subset of forget-set examples and on retain or unrelated data is tested. The paper does not test every possible loosely related dataset or relearning protocol.
Representation metrics are used to analyze preservation or drift; no activation-direction ablation is performed.
The reported quantization attack is Int4 on one unlearned model and setting; other bit widths and settings are not tested.
Paraphrased prompts, a fixed jailbreak prefix, and five-shot in-context demonstrations are tested. Other languages and prompt attacks are not tested in this recovery comparison.
The paper compares additional unlearning methods under relearning, but does not test a counter-method against the full set of prompting, quantization, and other attacks.

source_check.notes: F.Acc is forget-set accuracy and no held-out split is stated, so 'held-out' wording in the synthesis does not fit this study. Tables 11-12 (GA, LR 6e-6, N=100) are a setting the paper calls reversible catastrophic forgetting, so the prompt, quantization and retain/unrelated results come from a collapsed model. B.conflicts[7] does not list this difference. Table 15 names no model; Yi-6B is inferred. Section 3.1 says single unlearning uses N=1, while Tables 11-12 use N=100.

statements.correction: Yi-6B GA, LR 6e-6, N=100: relearning on forget-set data at 10/30/60/100% of forget-set size gives F.Acc 67.28/75.77/77.13/79.20 from 0.00; original 78.90 (Table 12). F.Acc is forget-set accuracy. No held-out split is stated.
statements.problem: Numbers are right, but it calls this study's F.Acc 'held-out'. The text never says scoring leaves out relearned facts, and the 100% budget relearns the whole forget set. The conditions line ('facts not in the relearning set') does not fit this study either.

statements.correction: Unrelated-data relearning on Yi-6B GA (LR 6e-6, N=100): 0.02/6.48/38.83/65.66 at 10/30/60/100% budgets vs original 78.90 (Table 12). The authors call it slower and less sample-efficient than forget-set data.
statements.problem: Numbers are right, but 38.83 and 65.66 at the 60% and 100% budgets are substantial recovery, not 'no or weak'. Only the 10% and 30% budgets fit the headline. The record's verdict for this group is limits_scope.

statements.correction: Retain-set relearning: 0.05/11.24/45.24/75.86 at 10/30/60/100% budgets vs original 78.90 (Table 12).
